messages.author: a12ca8b2d07f7b5f
messages.subject: Lavaan in R Studio
parts:
I had been running SEM models using lavaan on R-Studio and suddenly, this is the message I get for a model I have run umpteen times before: fit <- cfa(SM1.model, data=SM.csv)
Error in cfa(SM1.model, data = SM.csv) : 
  could not find function "cfa"
Error in summary(fit, standardized = TRUE) : object 'fit' not found

If I load the SEM package as well, this is the error message I get: Error in file(file, "r") : cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning message:
In file(file, "r") : cannot open file 'my model is specified here' File name too long. So, it is reading my model as filename even though I have the apostophe in place for model specification. Furthermore, it says: Error in summary(fit, standardized = TRUE) : object 'fit' not found.

I am unable to find the 'fit' function (I used it before); I see fitted, fitmeasures, but no 'fit.'

I have uninstalled and reinstalled R-studio a couple of times to no avail. What am I missing suddenly? Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Lavaan in R Studio
parts:
Can't say why it's not finding the cfa() function (have you loaded lavaan)?

But it's not looking for 'fit' as a function. fit is an object you're
trying to create with the cfa() function. Since the cfa() call fails,
fit is never created, and can't be found by summary()

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Lavaan in R Studio
parts: could someone please help me with how to export my lavaan output to Excel or Word in original format?

Other than copy/pasting manually, you could use RMarkdown to export output to Word, or you could use the semTools::clipboard() function to copy lavaan's Console output to Excel in pretty columns.  The latter seems to have stopped working on MacOS, but I think it still works on Windows.
